name: BellRing Brands, Inc.

profile.description: BellRing Brands sells convenient nutrition products, chiefly Premier Protein ready-to-drink shakes and powders and Dymatize sports nutrition powders. It was spun out of Post Holdings in 2019. Revenue grew from $988M in FY2020 to $2.32B in FY2025. In FY2026 growth slowed to 1-4%, gross margin fell sharply on whey costs and inventory charges, and the stock fell from a 52-week high of $33.56 to about $9. Michael Axelrod succeeded retiring CEO Darcy Horn Davenport on July 29, 2026.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): BellRing scaled Premier Protein and Dymatize to a 5-year revenue CAGR of 18.6% ($988M to $2.32B) through distribution and line extensions rather than new categories [2]. The Q3 FY2026 release mentions no new product launches [3]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI savings were found in filings or releases [3]. Market Share (2/2): The CEO calls Premier Protein 'the clear leader in ready-to-drink shakes', and Dymatize grew 26.7% in Q3 FY2026. Premier itself grew only 0.7% while an investor suit alleges rising protein-shake competition [3][6]. Pipeline (0/2): No named next-generation products with launch dates were disclosed [3]. R&D (0/1): R&D is reported at 0% of revenue [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): BellRing has no formal mission or purpose statement on its website, only the tagline 'Changing Lives with Good Energy!' The more specific mission ('use science to unlock human potential') belongs to the Dymatize brand [7]. Community Impact (1/2): The Impact section cites donations, volunteer days and a 2025 Impact Report, but names no specific program or dollar amount [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found, and the CEO who led the company since its 2019 IPO retired in 2026 [5]. Insider Buying (1/2): Director Shawn Conway bought 2,022 shares at $9.89 on September 8, 2026 (about $20,000), but other insider activity is routine awards, so buying is roughly neutral [8].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored 6/10 (weighted 6.17 of 10). Several metrics score full marks: the 5-year revenue CAGR of 18.6% (1.0, 2x), the forward P/E of 6.91 (1.0) and the forward PEG of 0.25 (1.0, 2x) [1][2][4]. YoY revenue growth of 4.2% scores 0.81 and the 7.3% TTM profit margin scores 0.36 [1][3]. D/E and ROE are not calculable because stockholders' equity is negative (book value -$4.01/share against $1.14B of long-term debt), so both score 0 (ROE at 2x) [3][4]. Liquidity floor cleared: $9.06 x 3,771,811 shares = $34.2M daily [1].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): BellRing sells physical protein shakes and powders through Costco, Walmart, Amazon and other retailers. AI cannot substitute for nutrition consumers drink, and no analyst cites AI as a risk to the protein category [3]. Its real risks are input costs (whey) and retail competition, not AI. AI Opportunity (0/1): BellRing reports no AI-related revenue or AI initiatives [3].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens BellRing has played a finite, quarter-driven game. Its growth story depended on retailer inventory builds that a pending securities class action says masked true demand [6]. Management spent $133.1M buying back stock at an average $27.41 in the first nine months of FY2026, versus about $9 today [3]. No articulated cause guides the company. The orderly CEO handoff and Dymatize's 26.7% growth are the main stabilizing signals [3][5].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Changing Lives with Good Energy!' is a marketing tagline, not a cause, and BellRing has no corporate mission statement [7]. Dymatize's 'use science to unlock human potential' is more inspiring but belongs to one brand and does not shape BellRing's strategy [7].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The CEO transition was orderly. Davenport announced her retirement in February 2026, the company stated there was no dispute over operations, and she stayed on as an advisor after Axelrod took over on July 29, 2026 [5]. No layoffs or culture red flags surfaced, and no evidence of exceptional trust or empowerment was found.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management messaging emphasizes being 'the clear leader in ready-to-drink shakes' rather than learning from fast-growing rivals [3]. Shareholders are suing over undisclosed competitive pressure, which suggests competitors were downplayed rather than studied [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Since its 2019 spin from Post, BellRing has shifted its mix toward Dymatize powders and broadened retail distribution, which are incremental adaptations [2][3]. The company remains concentrated in Premier Protein shakes, with no transformative pivot.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Leadership prioritized buybacks ($133.1M at $27.41 average in nine months) while long-term debt rose to $1.14B and equity stayed negative [3]. That is financial engineering rather than long-term capability-building. The alleged reliance on retailer stockpiling to report growth is the opposite of courage [6].

investment_thesis: BellRing is now priced for distress despite category leadership. At $9.06 the stock trades at 6.9x forward earnings and 6.4x EV/EBITDA, with a TTM free cash flow yield of about 21% [1][4]. FY2026 guidance still calls for $2.335-$2.375B of net sales (+1-3%) and $275-$295M of adjusted EBITDA [3]. Premier Protein remains the leading RTD shake and Dymatize grew 26.7% in Q3 [3]. About $28M of FY2026 EBITDA pressure comes from one-time inventory charges ($11.3M ingredient quality, $10.0M excess bottles) that should not recur [3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is a structurally weaker business with a levered balance sheet. Q3 FY2026 gross margin collapsed to 28.6% from 35.4%, adjusted EBITDA fell 35% to $78.3M, and adjusted EPS halved to $0.30, as whey costs and promotions hit [3]. Long-term debt of $1.14B sits against negative equity, while inventories swelled to $480.6M from $330.4M [3]. Denha v. BellRing (S.D.N.Y.) alleges growth was driven by retailer stockpiling; the stock fell 33% on August 5, 2025 and has kept falling [6]. A new CEO from smaller snack companies must now rebuild credibility [5].
key_catalysts: New CEO Michael Axelrod's first strategic plan alongside FY2027 guidance in November 2026, which could reset expectations from the depressed $9 share price [3][5]
Roll-off of about $28M of FY2026 one-time inventory charges and easing whey protein costs restoring gross margin toward the 35% level of the prior year [3]
Continued Dymatize momentum (+26.7% in Q3 FY2026) diversifying growth beyond Premier Protein shakes [3]
key_risks: Securities class action (Denha v. BellRing Brands, No. 26-cv-00575, S.D.N.Y.) alleging sales growth came from retailer inventory stockpiling, which could bring damages and further credibility loss [6]
Balance sheet: $1.14B of long-term debt, negative stockholders' equity and inventories up 45% to $480.6M limit flexibility if EBITDA keeps falling [3]
Margin erosion from whey costs and promotional competition in RTD shakes: Q3 adjusted gross margin fell to 27.7% from 35.1% and Premier Protein grew just 0.7% [3]
